note: Diagnostic codes owned by nostdb-spec. A code marked prd_required appears in the required list in docs/PRD.md section 28 of the root superproject. The owner is the repository whose implementation raises the code, which is not always the Engine: the workspace verifier compares each owner's vocabulary against the codes owned by it. Codes are stable identifiers: rename none of them.

codes.summary: A catalog breaks a rule decidable by reading it. Reports every problem found, not the first. A stale entry target is not one of them.
The catalog_version is not one this build reads.
A change set breaks a rule decidable without a database. Reports every problem found, not the first.
The change_set_version is not one this build reads. A change set is not preserved and rewritten, so part of one is not read.
Two declarations in the same scope share a name.
Two declarations claim the same opaque record identifier.
Two link declarations claim the same alias.
Two link declarations canonicalize to the same source locator.
A property block sets the same key twice.
Two schema declarations share a name.
An integer literal does not fit in a signed 64-bit value.
A datetime literal is not a valid RFC 3339 timestamp.
A contribution or evidence block omits a required key, states an unknown key, or gives a key a value of the wrong shape.
A stated record identifier is not a kind prefix followed by a canonical UUID.
A float literal is not finite, or a confidence score falls outside 0.0 through 1.0.
The input does not match the .nost grammar. Carries a source range.
Two schemas named by one record declare the same field key with different types.
A record does not satisfy a schema it names. Schema validation is soft, so this is a warning; an explicit Constraint is hard.
The database advanced while the .nost file did not, so the file no longer describes the database and must be regenerated explicitly.
An aliased endpoint names an alias no link declaration defines.
An endpoint names a declaration that cannot be resolved. The Engine creates a Placeholder rather than an Edge with a null endpoint.
The @nost version header names a language version this implementation does not support.
Both the database and the .nost file changed from the same baseline. Neither representation is modified.
The container is structurally invalid: bad magic, failed checksum, truncation, an out-of-bounds section, or overlapping sections.
The container declares a format version this implementation does not support.
The container exceeds a bounded-parsing limit, so it is refused without allocating from an untrusted length.
The query is inside the subset but meaningless, such as an unbound variable or mismatched UNION columns. Nothing executed.
The query uses a construct outside the declared subset. Nothing executed, and no alternative was guessed.
A write named a record belonging to a linked source. Linked records are read-only from the root transaction, so nothing was modified.
Recursive link traversal reached a canonical source it had already opened. The cycle is cut and the result is partial.
Recursive link traversal reached a configured depth or database limit. Traversal stops there and the result is partial.
A declared link could not be opened. The declaration stays, the reachable results are returned, and the summary reports the result as partial.
A start request found a healthy daemon. Reported as the outcome of a start, not as a failure, because starting something already started is what the caller wanted.
The client and the daemon support no common server_protocol_version. The refusal names the versions this side has.
A settings link entry names a source no link declaration in the database carries. The entry is ignored.
A settings document is malformed: a missing or non-positive version, a wrong field type, an unsafe database path, an aliased or duplicate link entry, or a negative limit.
A settings document names a version this implementation cannot read, or cannot write without losing a field it does not understand.
